title: Accident reporting
summary: Covers what to do and know in an accident or emergency, dealing with injuries, RIDDOR reporting duties and keeping the accident book.

sections.heading: Being ready for an emergency
paragraphs: Know the procedure for summoning the emergency services where you are working and know your immediate contact point. Time is essential, so use your mobile phone to summon help rather than walking around the site looking for a phone.
Always attend safety briefings and updates provided by your company, because the information may suddenly and without warning become critical.
bullets: Information the emergency services need: address of site, nature of emergency (to get the correct service), exact location of the emergency, your name and phone number, name of person injured (if applicable), exact injuries and whether they are conscious
Understand how and when to set off an alarm and know the alarm signal
Know escape routes on your construction site
Be aware of the emergency meeting points on site

sections.heading: Dealing with injuries
paragraphs: If you discover someone who has been injured, follow the procedure in order.

sections.heading: RIDDOR
paragraphs: Serious incidents must be reported under RIDDOR (Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations). These regulations put duties on employers, the self-employed and people in control of work premises (the Responsible Person) to report serious workplace accidents, occupational diseases and specified dangerous occurrences (near misses).

An injury that keeps an employee or self-employed person away from work, or unable to do their normal duties, for more than seven consecutive days must be reported. The day of the accident is not counted, but weekends and rest days are.
bullets: Reportable: deaths and injuries, occupational diseases, dangerous occurrences, gas incidents
Types of reportable injury: deaths, major injuries, injuries resulting in more than 7 days off work
The report must be made within 15 days of the accident

sections.heading: The accident book
paragraphs: All accidents, whether or not they fall within RIDDOR, must be recorded in the company accident book. A company employing 10 or more persons must keep one under social security law; for fewer than 10 persons it is recommended.
bullets: Details to include: name and address of injured person, date and time of accident, location of accident, cause and nature of injury, name and address of person recording the details
RIDDOR records must include: date and method of reporting, date, time and place of the event, personal details of those involved, a brief description of the nature of the event or disease

flashcards.front: Why should you use your mobile phone in an emergency?
flashcards.back: Time is essential; you do not have time to walk around the site looking for a phone.

flashcards.front: What information do the emergency services require?
flashcards.back: Address of site, nature of emergency, exact location, your name and phone number, name of injured person, and their exact injuries and whether conscious.

flashcards.front: Why must you always attend safety briefings?
flashcards.back: The information given may suddenly and without warning become critical.

flashcards.front: What is the procedure when you discover an injured person?
flashcards.back: Make self safe, make area safe, administer first aid where appropriate, contact emergency services, contact nominated first aid person, contact supervisor.
Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations.
Employers, the self-employed and people in control of work premises (the Responsible Person).

flashcards.front: What must be reported under RIDDOR?
flashcards.back: Deaths and injuries, occupational diseases, dangerous occurrences and gas incidents.

flashcards.front: How long off work makes an injury reportable?
flashcards.back: More than seven consecutive days, not counting the day of the accident but including weekends and rest days.

flashcards.front: Within how many days must a RIDDOR report be made?
Which accidents must go in the accident book?
flashcards.back: All accidents, whether or not they fall within the scope of RIDDOR.

flashcards.front: When must a company keep an accident book by law?
flashcards.back: If it employs 10 or more persons, under social security law. For fewer than 10 it is recommended.

flashcards.front: What details go in an accident book entry?
flashcards.back: Name and address of injured person, date and time, location, cause and nature of injury, and name and address of the person recording it.

quiz.q: What is the first step when you discover someone who has been injured?
options: Contact the nominated first aid person
quiz.why: The procedure begins with making yourself safe, then making the area safe.

quiz.q: Which step comes straight after making yourself safe when dealing with an injury?
quiz.why: The order is make self safe, make area safe, then administer first aid where appropriate.

quiz.q: How long must an injury keep someone off work to be reportable under RIDDOR?
quiz.why: Injuries leading to more than seven consecutive days away from work or unable to perform normal duties must be reported.

quiz.q: Within how many days of the accident must the RIDDOR report be made?
quiz.why: The report must be made within 15 days of the accident.

quiz.q: When counting the seven days for a reportable injury, which statement is correct?
options: The day of the accident is counted and weekends are excluded
The day of the accident is not counted, but weekends and rest days are
Weekends and rest days are not counted
quiz.why: The day of the accident is not counted but weekends and rest days are included.

quiz.q: From how many employees is a company required to keep an accident book under social security law?
quiz.why: If a company employs 10 or more persons it must keep an accident book under social security law.

quiz.q: Which of these is a reason to use a mobile phone to summon help in an emergency?
options: It is cheaper than other phones
Walking around the site looking for a phone wastes time
It records the accident for RIDDOR
quiz.why: Time is essential and you do not have time to walk around the site looking for a phone.

quiz.q: Which of these would the emergency services require from you?
options: The name of your employer's insurer
The exact location of the emergency
quiz.why: They require address of site, nature and exact location of the emergency, your name and number, and details of the injured person.

quiz.q: Which of these should be recorded in the accident book?
quiz.why: Details include name and address of injured person, date and time, location, cause and nature of injury, and recorder's details.

quiz.q: Which accidents must be recorded in the company accident book?
options: Only those causing more than seven days off work
All accidents, whether or not they fall under RIDDOR
quiz.why: All accidents, whether or not they fall within the scope of RIDDOR, must be recorded.
